verdict.rationale: Appwrite documents an official MCP server, including a hosted version bundled in Claude Code and Codex plugins with one OAuth sign-in, so LLM clients like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop can operate on an Appwrite project directly through its API. That makes natural-language operation a first-party supported path, but only through an external AI client; the evidence shows no native natural-language interface in the product itself. Missing for 10: a built-in natural-language console or assistant, documentation of which operations the MCP server exposes, and independent hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation.
